claims.text: Polycrystalline titanium alloys can exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
The temperature dependence of plastic deformation in polycrystalline titanium alloys is caused by thermally activated dislocation motion.
Temperature-dependent dislocation behavior can be studied using in situ TEM or XRD.
Ti-6Al-4V is an example of the proposed polycrystalline titanium-alloy material.
The proposed material has an approximately 10 micrometer grain size.
The proposed intervention is uniaxial tensile deformation at 25, 100, 200, and 300 degrees Celsius and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
In situ TEM or XRD during deformation can reveal microstructural changes.
Dislocation density and arrangement are the structural mediators of the proposed behavior.
The operative deformation mechanisms are thermally activated dislocation glide and climb.
Yield stress at 25 degrees Celsius will be 20% higher than at 300 degrees Celsius.
Ductility at 25 degrees Celsius will be lower than at 300 degrees Celsius.
The yield stress of the polycrystalline titanium alloy at 25 degrees Celsius is approximately 900 MPa.
Grain size, impurities, and testing conditions may influence the relationship between temperature and dislocation behavior.
A measured 25 degrees Celsius yield stress outside 810–990 MPa would falsify the hypothesis.
